"Lenny" is the tenth and final track on the first Stevie Ray Vaughan album Texas Flood. The song is in 4/4 time and notated in the key of E flat major (but instruments are tuned down a half-step). It is played very slowly and freely, with Vaughan alternating between jazz-inflected chords and solo runs. The main chord featured in the song is a movable Major 6th chord in which Stevie Ray Vaughan applies moderate vibrato by use of tremolo bar. The solos incorporate both the E major scale, E minor Pentatonic scale, and E Minor Blues scale. The style is influenced by Jimi Hendrix ballads like "Little Wing" and "Angel".[1] The song itself was written and named for his wife at the time, Lenora. Vaughan also named one of his guitars "Lenny", which he used to play this song and also "Riviera Paradise". The song was often played at live shows.

So 'Moneda de Reserva' is a brand, but not a winery. Much like 'Charles Shaw' (from Trader Joes). I'm not sure how Moneda de Reserva works; but I know about Charles Shaw, and I suspect the story here is roughly the same.

Wineries wind up with extra stock all the time. A contract they expected to come through may not have; or they planned for a standard loss of stock but wound up losing much less. To move this wine they have a few choices:

+ Let it go to waste
+ Release it at a lower price
+ Sell it to a different brand

Really good wineries, with a brand that hinges on quality and high price, don't want to put their bottles on shelves for cheap, even if they have excess product. So Trader Joe's buys these up and puts them out under the Charles Shaw brand. Sometimes the wine is pretty terrible (like vinegar), and sometimes it's damned good; but it's always cheap.

I suspect that this $6 Walmart Wine probably has excess product in it, which is sitting on the same shelf for $35 or $40.

I also see a lot of comments hating on "wine snobs". While I can't tell the difference between a $35 bottle and a $200 bottle, I can damn sure tell the difference between a $5 bottle and a $35 bottle. If you've got friends and cash, have a tasting for yourself: you and 5 friends each buy a $5 bottle and a $30 bottle (make sure they're all different brands) and order them. There will probably be a cheap one that beats out an expensive one, but for the most part the $5s will be lower.
